question: A daily customer-insight digest that used to be quick now takes far longer and uses much more of the team's allowance than it did six months ago, although the tier it runs on has never changed. What should the team do first?
options: A) Move the digest up to the deepest-reasoning tier, on the basis that stronger answers should need fewer re-runs each morning.
B) Spread the digest across several colleagues' accounts, so that the daily allowance draw is shared out rather than falling on just one.
C) Move the digest down to the fastest and cheapest tier straight away and see whether the daily output is still good enough.
D) Look at how the digest itself has grown, in the length of what is fed in and the number of re-runs, before changing tier at all.
correct_answers: D) Look at how the digest itself has grown, in the length of what is fed in and the number of re-runs, before changing tier at all.
explanations: Escalating adds cost to a task that is already consuming too much, and depth does not address inputs that have quietly grown. It is as likely to worsen the allowance problem as to fix the re-runs.

Spreading the draw across accounts hides the consumption rather than reducing it, leaves the underlying growth undiagnosed, and is likely to conflict with how the organisation expects allowances to be used.

Changing tier is a plausible eventual answer, but doing it first treats a symptom. If the digest is now processing far more material and being re-run repeatedly, a lighter tier will simply do the bloated task less well.

Correct. Nothing about the tier has changed, so the growth is in the task. Understanding how much longer the inputs are and how often the digest is being re-run identifies the real cause before any tier decision is made.
